items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The change is small and clear. `if queryset.query.is_sliced: raise ValueError("Prefetch querysets cannot use slices.")` follows the same style as the existing raw/values check, and black formatting was applied.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The guard itself is tidy, but it adds a new restriction in the wrong place: Prefetch.__init__ in query.py, instead of a shared helper in related_descriptors.py. It closes off the feature the issue asks for, and hidden tests will need it removed.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: It replaces a confusing TypeError raised later with a clear ValueError at construction time. Nothing is swallowed. But a valid use case is now rejected instead of supported.

items.name: Per-parent slice semantics for open/bounded slices
items.name_zh: 开放/有界切片按父对象分区
items.evidence: There are no per-parent slice semantics. Prefetch now raises "Prefetch querysets cannot use slices." No Window/RowNumber partition, no low/high mark handling. Result: F2P 0/4 (test_foreignkey_reverse, test_m2m_forward and others fail).
